svg.title: Why the radius must be the square root of the value
svg.desc: Two wedges, A worth 1 and B worth 4, drawn twice. On the left the radius equals the value, so B is four times as long and has sixteen times the area of A, which exaggerates the difference. On the right the radius is the square root of the value, so B is twice as long and has four times the area, which matches the data.
